messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Processing sleep with GGIR
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to process sleep data with g.part4 on GGIR package, but something looks wrong to me. I hope any of you can have a look on this to get some guide.

I attach the sleeplog file for subject 001, and the ms4.out milestone data generated for that subject.

Here the code used:

g.part4(datadir = datadir, metadatadir = metadatadir, f0 = 1, f1 = 1, idloc = 2, loglocation = loglocation, coln1 = 2, sleeplogidnum = FALSE, do.visual = TRUE, relyonsleeplog = TRUE)

Doubt 1: I defined argument "relyonsleeplog" as TRUE because we insisted to the participants to do it correctly, so we want to use these hours as bedtime onset and offset. However in the milestone attached, the variable "sleeplog used" is FALSE for each night, so, is it not using the times that we provided? Or can we assume bedtime as the time between "sleeplog_onset" and "sleeplog_wake", and sleeptime as the time between "acc_onset" and "acc_wake"?

Doubt 2: As you can see in the sleeplog, night 1 onset is at 23:54:00. But in the milestone, "sleeplog_onset" for the night 1 is 20.55, that would mean more or less 20:30 if we consider this variable as the number of hours since the previous midnight. So, is it not reading correctly the sleeplog? Can you see any format error or similar in the sleeplog?

Hope any of you can help me with these questions.

Thank you a lot in advance,
Jairo

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Processing sleep with GGIR
parts:
Hi Jairo,

This indicates that the participant ID is not recognised from the sleeplog.

Note that the participant id as stored in the csv output from part2 should match the participant id in the sleep log used for part4.
The participant identifier currently extracted from the accelerometer data seems to be: 001M (2015-02-10)RAW.csv.RData rather than 001M.

What could help is changing idloc=2 to idloc=1 as that will make that the id is extracted from the file header.

Cheers,
Vincent
